answer: One identity stakes a 70-credit bond and claims a saffron-marked bridge post. Each epoch it crosses the next span and files a fresh cipher log; the bridge table is public, so auditors recompute every crossing. A missing, copied, or rented log burns the bond. The kth fake pays 40+6(k-1), since farther posts mean longer spans; forging 1,000 identities costs 3,037,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. An honest agent pays 40 once.
